Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)

Required findings: Patient must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Imaging must demonstrate ANY of the following:

- Degenerative spondylolisthesis without spondylolysis AND either dynamic segmental instability on flexion‑extension plain x‑rays OR a supine‑to‑upright translational shift >3 mm, OR Meyerding Grade II or higher spondylolisthesis.

- Spondylolisthesis with spondylolysis (isthmic) AND either Meyerding Grade I or II with radiographic evidence of progression, OR Meyerding Grade III or higher with ≥50 % anterior slippage or radiographic progression.
- Progressive spinal pain with documented progression of spondylolisthesis on serial imaging.
- Multi‑level spondylolysis evident on plain x‑rays.
- Post‑operative instability caused by facet joint excision exceeding 50 % bilaterally or ≥75 % of a single facet.
- Prior spinal decompression that resulted in iatrogenic spondylolisthesis.
Exception: If instability is identified intra‑operatively, imaging criteria are not required.
Documentation of nicotine‑free status: either never‑smoker or abstinent ≥6 weeks with objective cotinine test (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range.
Patient must be a candidate for lumbar decompression or lumbar corpectomy per CMM-608: Lumbar Decompression.
Anticipated iatrogenic instability must be present, demonstrated by ANY of the following intra‑operative or pre‑operative findings:
- Disruption of posterior elements due to facet joint excision >50 % bilaterally or ≥75 % of a single facet during decompression.
- Removal of the pars interarticularis that necessitates fusion for stability.
- Decompression performed for Meyerding Grade I or higher spondylolisthesis with associated foraminal stenosis.
- Complete or partial corpectomy involving removal of ≥1/3 of a vertebral body (not limited to osteophyte resection).
Documentation of nicotine‑free status: either never‑smoker or abstinent ≥6 weeks with objective cotinine test (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range.

Non-Indications: Patient is not a candidate for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608.

Imaging does not demonstrate any of the specified instability criteria (e.g., Meyerding Grade I spondylolisthesis without progression, translational shift ≤3 mm, facet excision <50 % bilaterally and <75 % unilaterally).
Absence of documented nicotine‑free status (no history of never‑smoking and no cotinine test confirming abstinence ≥6 weeks).
Instability is not anticipated or identified intra‑operatively and imaging criteria are unmet.
Procedure requested for spondylolisthesis without associated foraminal stenosis or without need for fusion (i.e., isolated low‑grade spondylolisthesis managed conservatively).
Important criteria & exceptions: Intra‑operative identification of instability waives the pre‑operative imaging requirements.
Patient must meet nicotine‑free criteria (never‑smoker or ≥6 weeks abstinent with normal cotinine test).
Eligibility is contingent upon prior determination that the patient is a candidate for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608.
Both actual and anticipated instability pathways are acceptable; only one set of criteria needs to be satisfied.
Documentation required: Clinical note confirming candidate status for lumbar decompression or corpectomy per CMM-608 (symptom description, neurological exam).
Flexion‑extension plain radiographs or supine and upright standing radiographs demonstrating translational shift >3 mm (if applicable).
Standard standing AP/Lateral radiographs with Meyerding grading of spondylolisthesis.
CT or MRI reports documenting facet joint resection extent, pars fracture, or corpectomy extent if relevant.
Prior operative reports if previous decompression or facet excision was performed.
Objective cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range confirming ≥6 weeks nicotine abstinence, or documented never‑smoker status.
Intra‑operative report documenting identified iatrogenic instability (if imaging criteria are not met).
